title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
summary: In a binary search tree, identify the lowest common ancestor of two specified nodes.
statement: In a binary search tree, identify the lowest common ancestor of two specified nodes. The LCA is the deepest node that has both specified nodes as descendants, including the nodes themselves as descendants.
constraints: The input contains 2–100 TreeNode objects with unique values from -10^9 through 10^9, arranged as a binary search tree.
p and q are different existing nodes selected by their values. Return the actual lowest common ancestor node from root; a node is its own descendant, and the input tree must remain unchanged.

hints: BST ordering tells you which single side can still contain both selected values.
If both values are smaller, move left; if both are larger, move right.
Stop at the first node whose value lies between p.val and q.val, including either endpoint.
Return that existing TreeNode, not a newly created node with the same value.
editorial: Walk down from the root while both targets remain strictly on one side. The first split point, or the first selected node encountered, is the deepest node containing both targets. The judge passes p and q as actual references within root and requires the returned identity while confirming that no link or value changed. The independent oracle finds both binary paths in the compact input and takes their longest common prefix.
